newsitem.title: DUBAI: Gulf dailies criticise Israeli settlement drive.
newsitem.headline: Gulf dailies criticise Israeli settlement drive.

text.p: Gulf Arab newspapers said on Friday that Israel's building drive in Arab East Jerusalem threatened to revive a Palestinian revolt and plunge the Middle East into violence.
The international community's failure to persuade Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to halt it only added salt to injury, they said.

"Netanyahu's actions, and the failure of the world community to do anything apart from talk...has left Palestinians with no choice but that of an intifada (uprising)," said Saudi Arabia's Arabic-language al-Jazira newspaper.
"This will force Netanyahu to rush back to Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat to seek help," it added.
Another Saudi paper, al-Yaum, said Netanyahu's move was "an evil setback that has put peace in the region at a crossroads."

"These daily Israeli moves are pushing towards an escalation of violence...Tel Aviv rulers, who are insisting on continuing this path, can only expect reactions they will not be envied for...." said Qatar's al-Sharq newspaper.
"Arab leaders are urged to take decisions they see as suitable to defend their causes regardless of what outside parties might think," wrote the United Arab Emirates' al-Khaleej daily.
"The United States has exposed its bias towards Israel... until when will the Arabs accept such humiliation?" it asked.
